Name: HD Core
Author: ParadoxQED
Description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]HDCore is a small framework that lets item icons in Stardew Valley use their [b]full texture resolution[/b] without changing how much space they take on screen.
Vanilla always draws an item icon from a hard-coded 16×16 slice of its texture and then scales that slice up 4×. A 64×64 texture therefore only ever shows its top-left corner. HDCore changes that single path: it samples the [b]whole texture[/b] for qualifying items, then scales it by "[/color]64 / texture size"[color=#d4d4d8], so the icon still occupies exactly one 64px grid cell.[/color]
[color=#D4D4D8]The result: 16×16 art looks identical to vanilla, 64×64 art is four times sharper, and both can sit side by side without one looking blurry next to the other.
HDCore does [b]not[/b] modify any vanilla or third-party assets. It is opt-in: a mod must declare a dependency on it and register its own texture ranges through a small API. Anything not registered renders exactly like vanilla.
Who it is for:[/color]

[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Players[/b] — install it and forget it. There is no config and no in-game menu. Mods that support HD icons simply look sharper.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Mod authors[/b] — a short registration gets your high-resolution icons displayed properly in inventories, shops, crafting menus and on the ground.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Install SMAPI 4.0.0 or later.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Download and unzip HDCore.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Put the "[/color]HDCore" folder into your "Stardew Valley/Mods" folder.[/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]To confirm it loaded, check your SMAPI log for a line containing [/color][HDCore][color=#d4d4d8].[/color]
[color=#D4D4D8]To uninstall, delete the "[/color]HDCore" [color=#d4d4d8]folder. Mods that relied on it fall back to vanilla rendering automatically, and no save data is touched.[/color]


[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Full-resolution icons, same footprint[/b] — qualifying textures are drawn from the whole image and scaled to a fixed 64px cell, so grid layout never changes.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]One consistent path everywhere[/b] — inventory, shops, crafting menu, BetterCrafting recipe grid, buff icons, held items and dropped-item debris all use the same scaling rule, so HD icons no longer become 4× giants in the world.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Furniture icons[/b] — non-square furniture art is fitted by its longest edge to 64px instead of overflowing its cell.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Weapons[/b] — weapon textures keep a downscaled copy for the 4× held/swing path (so a held weapon stays normal-sized) while the full-resolution original is used for menu icons.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Big craftables[/b] — square big-craftable icons are drawn as a one-cell-wide square anchored to the bottom of their footprint, instead of being stretched to twice their height by the vanilla 1:2 target rectangle.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Large-texture handling[/b] — only square item textures larger than 1024×1024 are area-averaged down to 1024 at load time; anything smaller is kept native.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Opt-in by design[/b] — unregistered mods, multi-frame atlases ("SpriteIndex != 0[/color][color=#D4D4D8]), 16×16 legacy art and UI textures are never touched.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Fail-safe patches[/b] — every patch is wrapped individually, so a single failed hook disables only that path and never interrupts the game.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b][/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/b] (required)[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]BetterCrafting[/b] (optional) — detected at runtime, its recipe grid is scaled automatically. HDCore never references its assembly directly.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]For mod authors[/b][/size]
HDCore is a framework; nothing is taken over automatically. To have your icons handled:
[list=1]
[*]Declare the dependency in your "manifest.json": 
"Dependencies": [  { "UniqueID": "ParadoxQED.HDCore", "MinimumVersion": "1.0.0", "IsRequired": true }][/*]
[*]Declare a matching interface in your own source. You do [b]not[/b] need to reference "HDCore.dll"— SMAPI proxies the API by member name: 
public interface IHdCoreApi{    bool IsApplied { get; }    int IconSize { get; }    int IndexedTextures { get; }    bool Register(string modUniqueId, string[] textureNamePatterns);}[/*]
[*]Register from "GameLaunched"— querying the API earlier returns null: 
var api = Helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<IHdCoreApi>("ParadoxQED.HDCore");api?.Register(ModManifest.UniqueID, new[] { "Mods/YourAuthor.YourMod/" });[/*]
[/list]Registration is rejected when the dependency is not declared in your manifest. Author your icons as [b]square and at least 64×64[/b] (68, 72, 96, 128 all work — they are scaled by actual size). If the source art is rectangular, pad the short edge up to the long one; never stretch it.


[size=4][b]Shout outs[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]The Stardew Valley modding community and the SMAPI team, for an API that makes this kind of surgical draw-path change possible.[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Everyone who reported blurry or oversized icons — those reports shaped the 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 fixes.[/color][/*]
[/list]

Manifest.Name: HD 图标引擎 (HDCore)
Manifest.Description: 高清物品图标引擎：贴图整图取样 + 屏幕上恒定 64px + 制作界面（含 BetterCrafting）同步缩放。只对「方形、边长 ≥64、SpriteIndex = 0」的物品贴图生效。1.2.0：修正建造物（bigCraftable）世界绘制——原版把 16×32 格子塞进 1:2 目标矩形，方形图标会被竖向拉成两倍高；改为一格宽正方形、底边贴格子底部，并补 Object.drawAsProp（放置预览）同口径。1.2.1：加载降采样阈值 256 → 1024（超限也只压到 1024），否则「短边补到长边」恢复出来的 288/359 图标会在加载时被压回 64。
Manifest.Author: ParadoxQED
